```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
options(scipen = 999)

# one colour per primer/barcode combination (5 combinations)
barcode_colours <- c("maroon4",
                     "steelblue4",
                     "lightskyblue",
                     "olivedrab1",
                     "darkolivegreen")
```

# Load consensus barcodes

One row per consensus sequence (`qseqid`), with the dataset, sample, barcode, primer set
and number of supporting reads (`readcount`) parsed from the sequence name.

```{r load-consensus-barcodes}
consensus_barcodes <- read_tsv("/Volumes/TOSHIBA/OrCA-seq_slurm/all_BLAST_top5.tsv", col_names = FALSE) %>%
  select(qseqid = X1, qseqs_length = X2) %>%
  mutate(
    # harmonise dataset names, then pull the pieces out of the sequence name
    qseqid    = gsub("BWplate", "Garden", qseqid),
    qseqid    = gsub("day", "Lakes", qseqid),
    dataset   = str_extract(qseqid, "Lakes[0-9]|Garden[0-9]"),
    readcount = as.numeric(str_extract(qseqid, "(?<=readcount_)[0-9]+")),

    # adapters are repeated per dataset, so pasting the dataset on keeps samples distinct
    sample = paste0(str_extract(qseqid, "SP27_[0-9]+_SP5_[0-9]+"), "_", dataset),

    # which barcode is this?
    barcode = case_when(
      grepl("28S", qseqid) ~ "28S",
      grepl("18S", qseqid) ~ "18S",
      TRUE                 ~ "COI"
    ),

    # which primers were used? (inferred from barcode and consensus length)
    primer_set = case_when(
      barcode == "COI" & qseqs_length <= 499  ~ "Sauron",
      barcode == "COI" & qseqs_length >= 500  ~ "Moorea",
      barcode == "28S" & qseqs_length <= 2499 ~ "18S+",
      barcode == "28S" & qseqs_length >= 2500 ~ "28S_solo",
      barcode == "18S"                        ~ "18S+",
      TRUE                                    ~ "?"
    ),
    primer_barcode = paste(barcode, ",", primer_set)
  ) %>%
  # the BLAST file has several hits per consensus; keep one row per consensus
  distinct(qseqid, primer_barcode, readcount, dataset, sample)
```
# Barcodes retained as reads are subsampled

If only a fraction of the reads had been kept, what proportion of the barcodes that currently
have at least 20x coverage would still have at least 20x?

A barcode with `readcount` reads has about `readcount * fraction` reads after subsampling,
so it stays covered if that is at least `min_coverage`.

```{r subsampling-retention, fig.height = 8, fig.width = 8}
min_coverage       <- 20                       # reads a barcode needs to count as "covered"
fractions_of_reads <- seq(1, 0, by = -0.01)    # 100% of reads down to 0% in 1% steps (fine grid = smooth curve)

# Barcodes below the threshold at full depth can't recover, so exclude them
# (this makes every curve start at 100%)
barcodes_covered_at_full_depth <- consensus_barcodes %>%
  filter(readcount >= min_coverage)

# For every barcode x fraction: reads left, and whether that is still enough
retention_by_subsampling <- expand_grid(barcodes_covered_at_full_depth,
                                        fraction_of_reads = fractions_of_reads) %>%
  mutate(reads_after_subsampling = readcount * fraction_of_reads,
         still_covered           = reads_after_subsampling >= min_coverage) %>%
  group_by(primer_barcode, dataset, fraction_of_reads) %>%
  summarise(n_barcodes_retained    = sum(still_covered),    # raw count still covered
            prop_barcodes_retained = mean(still_covered),   # proportion of barcodes still covered
            .groups = "drop")

ggplot(retention_by_subsampling,
       aes(x = fraction_of_reads, y = prop_barcodes_retained, colour = primer_barcode)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_x_continuous(transform = "reverse",              # full depth on the left
                     breaks    = seq(1, 0, by = -0.1),  # fewer ticks so labels don't collide
                     labels    = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_color_manual(values = barcode_colours) +
  labs(x      = "Reads retained after subsampling (% of full depth)",
       y      = paste0("Barcodes retained"),
       colour = "Primer / barcode") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +              # two legend rows so nothing is cut off
  facet_wrap(~dataset, nrow = 3)

ggplot(retention_by_subsampling,
       aes(x = fraction_of_reads, y = n_barcodes_retained, colour = primer_barcode)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_x_continuous(transform = "reverse",
                     breaks    = seq(1, 0, by = -0.1),
                     labels    = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +                   # start at 0, let the top float
  scale_color_manual(values = barcode_colours) +
  labs(x      = "Reads retained after subsampling (% of full depth)",
       y      = paste0("Number of barcodes with ≥", min_coverage, "x coverage"),
       colour = "Primer / barcode") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  facet_wrap(~dataset, nrow = 3, scales = "free_y")         # each dataset gets its own count range
```
